documented_expected_divergences: canopy_cover_expanded_matrix.all: known_divergent_scenario_scoped — calc_canopy_cover vs the manifested canopy_cover golden, with the per-species crown-width equation supplied explicitly from the tracked FOF_SPP.CSV. 12 of the 14 successful per-tree scenarios agree and 4 of the 5 emitted stand aggregates agree: measured maximum relative difference 1.02e-06 and maximum |diff| 8.32e-04 ft2. The rtol 2e-06 is evidence-based, not tuned: C++ SMT_CalcCrnCov uses the literal 3.14159 (fof_mrt.cpp:1634) where Python uses numpy.pi, a fixed relative difference of 8.4e-07 in an expression linear in that constant, plus the C++ side's float32 arithmetic. The atol 1e-04 is the golden's own output resolution (crown areas and percentages are written through fmt(v, 4)). The 2 diverging trees and 1 diverging stand are strict xfails under F-02: C++ returns 0 crown area as soon as f_Hgt <= 0, while Python excludes a tree only for dbh <= 0, so it credits a zero- or negative-height tree 30.229674 ft2. Python's DEFAULT species mapping (equation 39 for every species) is a separate, larger divergence characterised separately and never relied upon: measured 40 % to 70 % relative error against the real per-species equations. (gate0/04-findings.md:F-02; gate0/07-branch-traceability.csv BR-CCV-LRG, BR-CCV-SML, BR-CCV-ZERO, BR-CCV-OVL; tests/unit/cpp/test_tree_structure_parity.py::test_canopy_cover_per_tree_area_matches_cpp, ::test_canopy_cover_stand_percent_matches_cpp, ::test_canopy_cover_default_equation_mapping_matches_cpp)
